facts.text: Caberfae takes its name from the Scottish Gaelic cabar‑fèidh, meaning antler or stag’s head, a title given to an ancestor of the MacKenzies in 1255.
Caberfae Peaks, Michigan’s first destination ski area, opened in the 1930s when local enthusiasts and the U.S. Forest Service built the first ski run with a Ford Model A‑powered rope tow.
The Civilian Conservation Corps erected Caberfae’s inaugural ski run, “Number One,” on North Peak during 1936–1937, marking the start of the resort’s lift‑served legacy.
Today Caberfae Peaks also hosts a nine‑hole golf course that winds through forested slopes and spans ten bridges.
After the Great Depression, the ranch sold to the U.S., became part of Manistee National Forest, and now sits on mixed public and private land.
